title: A signal for biological timing
hook: Connect a hormonal signal with a target.

knows: Hormones can carry signals through the blood to target tissues.
doesNotKnow: The pineal gland secretes melatonin, which participates in circadian timing and reflects the light–dark cycle.

misconception: All hormones come from one gland and act on every cell.
objective: Identify the stated endocrine signal and its target in a simplified pathway.

claims.text: Question, diagram and explanation: Which pineal hormone helps signal timing of the light–dark cycle to the body? The pineal gland secretes melatonin, which participates in circadian timing and reflects the light–dark cycle.
The diagram shows one selected source–target pathway, not all hormone effects or feedback loops.
Recall: In the stated example, which source releases Melatonin into the circulation? The pineal gland secretes melatonin, which participates in circadian timing and reflects the light–dark cycle.
